metadata.name: Fintech Payment API Platform
metadata.product_idea: Developer-friendly payment API for emerging market fintechs
metadata.description: Golden set reference for Fintech B2B products with API-first approach

state.product_idea: Developer-friendly payment API platform enabling fintechs in emerging markets to integrate multiple local payment methods with a single API

executive_summary.tagline: One API for every payment method in emerging markets
executive_summary.problem_statement: Fintechs in emerging markets must integrate 10-15 different local payment providers, each with unique APIs, compliance requirements, and reconciliation processes. This costs 6-12 months of engineering time and ongoing maintenance burden.
executive_summary.solution_overview: PayBridge provides a unified API that abstracts complexity of local payment methods across Africa, Southeast Asia, and Latin America, handling compliance, reconciliation, and settlement automatically.
executive_summary.value_proposition: Reduce payment integration time from 6 months to 2 weeks with a single API that handles local compliance and reconciliation automatically.
target_users: Technical founders at Series A-B fintechs
Product managers launching in new markets
executive_summary.target_market_size: TAM: $15B (global payment infrastructure). SAM: $3B (emerging market fintech payment solutions). SOM: $300M (Africa and Southeast Asia).
key_differentiators: Single API for 50+ local payment methods
executive_summary.competitive_landscape: Competing with Flutterwave, Paystack, and regional players. Differentiated by multi-region coverage and developer experience.
executive_summary.funding_required: $5M Series A for expansion to 5 additional markets and team scaling
executive_summary.revenue_model: Transaction-based pricing: 1.5% + $0.10 per transaction, with volume discounts
executive_summary.financial_projections: Year 1: $2M revenue, $150M TPV. Year 3: $15M revenue, $1B TPV.
executive_summary.expected_roi: 8x ROI by Year 3 based on transaction volume growth
top_risks: Regulatory changes in target markets could require rapid adaptation
Payment provider API instability in emerging markets
Competition from Stripe expanding to emerging markets
executive_summary.regulatory_summary: PCI DSS Level 1 compliance required. Local money transmission licenses needed in each market. AML/KYC requirements vary by country.
executive_summary.gtm_strategy: Developer-led growth starting with Nigeria and Kenya, expand to Southeast Asia in Year 2
key_milestones: Launch in Nigeria and Kenya with 10 payment methods (Month 3)

key_decisions.decision: Priority market for Southeast Asia expansion
key_decisions.recommendation: Indonesia first due to largest fintech ecosystem and clearer regulatory path

segments_examined: Series A fintech founders in Nigeria
Engineering leads at Southeast Asian neobanks
research_scope.observation_context: Conducted 20 customer interviews, analyzed integration documentation from 15 payment providers, reviewed fintech community discussions.
known_gaps: Limited data on Latin American market
Need more interviews with enterprise fintechs

job_to_be_done.trigger_situation: Fintech launches new market or adds new payment method to existing product
job_to_be_done.underlying_goal: Enable customers to pay using their preferred local method without engineering overhead
job_to_be_done.success_definition: Payment integration live in production with <1% failure rate

existing_solutions: Direct integration with each payment provider
friction_points: Each provider has unique API and error handling
Settlement timing varies from days to weeks
current_behaviour.why_problem_persists: Regional players optimize for local market, no true multi-region solution exists with developer-first approach.

pain_signals.description: Payment integrations take 3-6 months of engineering time
pain_signals.evidence_detail: Direct quotes from 8 fintech CTOs in customer interviews
pain_signals.impact: Delayed market launches and lost revenue opportunities

pain_signals.description: Reconciliation errors cause 2-5% of transactions to be disputed

pain_signals.description: Compliance monitoring requires dedicated team member
pain_signals.impact: High fixed cost especially for early-stage companies

uncomfortable_insights.insight: Many fintechs would accept higher transaction fees for faster integration and better reliability

what_customers_dont_care_about.reality: Most fintechs build custom checkout experiences, need API only

open_questions.question: What is the acceptable latency for payment confirmation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines architecture decisions for real-time vs async processing

Percentage of time API returns successful responses

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Payment provider API changes without notice

technical_architecture.system_overview: Multi-region payment processing platform with PCI DSS compliant infrastructure
technical_architecture.architecture_style: Event-driven microservices with CQRS for reconciliation

key_components.name: API Gateway
key_components.purpose: Single entry point for all API requests with rate limiting and auth

key_components.name: Payment Orchestrator
key_components.purpose: Routes payments to appropriate provider and handles state management

key_components.name: Reconciliation Service
key_components.technology: Python with pandas for data processing
interfaces: SFTP for settlement files, internal APIs

data_architecture.cache_layer: Redis for idempotency and rate limiting

technical_architecture.scalability_approach: Multi-region deployment with traffic routing based on payment geography
technical_architecture.deployment_strategy: Canary deployments with automatic rollback on error rate increase

architecture_diagrams.name: Payment Flow
architecture_diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    Client->>API Gateway: Initiate Payment
    API Gateway->>Orchestrator: Route Payment
    Orchestrator->>Provider: Process Payment
    Provider-->>Orchestrator: Confirmation
    Orchestrator-->>Client: Webhook
